waiting.title: 42040 Fire Plane: the hatch group onto its pins
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. The hatch behind the engine, with its lever group, is drawn 2 LDU off its two pins, so the whole group hangs on nothing. The correction moves it 2 LDU onto the pins.
waiting.effect: Function 3 (the hatch flips forward to fill the tank) goes from partly to working.
waiting.confidence: The worker rates it medium. Claude has not looked at the booklet pages.

waiting.title: 42093 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1: an 8-tooth gear on the engine shaft
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. The shaft that drives the engine has a 12-tooth gear where step 2 of the instructions puts an 8-tooth gear. The parts list has two 8-tooth and three 12-tooth gears; the file has one and four. The correction removes the 12-tooth gear and adds the 8-tooth gear in its place.
waiting.effect: The new gear meshes the crankshaft's gear, so pushing the car turns the crankshaft. The pistons still do not move, so function 1 stays skipped.
waiting.confidence: The worker rates it high. Claude checked the mesh in the viewer, not the booklet page.

waiting.title: 42099 4x4 X-treme Off-Roader: the rear differential's side gears onto their line
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. In the rear differential, the two side gears are drawn 3 LDU off the casing's line, so neither sits on its half shaft and Kinebrick reads the differential as locked. The correction moves both 3 LDU onto the line, where the front differential has them.
waiting.effect: The rear differential turns. The scores do not change (4 functions work, 3 partly): the halves of the rear CV joints come apart instead, a fault that is with the solver owner.
waiting.confidence: High. The worker looked at the booklet page: its 1:1 picture of the differential has the side gears facing each other on the casing's line. Every other differential in the 190 models has its side gears on the line.

waiting.title: 42099, 42041 and 8274: the differential casing stands still when one wheel is turned by hand
waiting.what: A change to four function lists. The 42099’s functions 5 and 6 and the 42041’s function 2 turn one wheel by hand with the model lifted, and the other wheel of the axle turns the opposite way. Each list names its differential casing among the parts that move. On the 42099 the casing’s ring gear meshes the pinion from the motor, which stands still, so the casing is held. On the 42041 the casing drives the V8, and with the truck lifted the free wheel is the easy way, so the casing stands; the function’s own words say the other wheel turns the opposite way. On the 8274 (function 4) the casing’s own 24 teeth mesh the reel drive’s gear, which the function holds, so the casing is held too. The change moves each casing from the parts that move to the parts that stay.
waiting.effect: 42099: none on the scores yet; both functions are partly, and with the change they ask for what a differential does. 42041: function 2 keeps working. Without the change it would go from works to partly once it is checked lifted, so its lifted mark is held back until you sign. 8274: function 4 is partly now, with the casing rightly still; with the change it should work, checked when you sign.
waiting.confidence: High. The 42099’s booklet step 140 shows the casing’s ring on the motor’s pinion; the 42041’s function words say the wheels turn opposite ways, which only happens with the casing still. The same change was made to the 42039’s function 2.

waiting.title: Two suspension functions: the list names the wrong part
waiting.what: Two changes to function lists, found by the worker while tracing suspension functions that do not work. In each, the model moves as the booklet shows, but the list asks for something else.
waiting.effect: The 42039’s function 6 goes from doesn’t work to works (tried by the worker). The 8261’s function 3 should go from partly to works; it is checked when you sign.
waiting.confidence: High for both: each follows from how the parts are joined in the booklet step linked.

rows.says: The control is two parts on the rear drive shafts, which can always spin, so pushing them never moves the suspension. The change makes the two lower arms the control (p61 and p63). Pushed there, each arm swings and the shock absorbers’ rods move.

links.label: Booklet p. 8 (hubs on the arms, step 12)

rows.says: The list says the pivot axle p55 stays still. The axle goes through the axle holes of both bent beams of the arm and through round holes in the frame, so it turns with the arm. The change moves p55 from the parts that stay to the parts that move.

waiting.title: Five audit rows where the booklet and the model agree by trial
waiting.what: Changes to our function lists. The worker set each control the way the booklet says and ran it in the model. A sign-off fixes the directions in the list; on the 42052 and the 42070 it does not make the functions that fail for other reasons work.

rows.says: Gear 1 is the 1:1 path, gear 2 the 8-to-24 path.
Handle forward and down = gear 1, level = neutral, up and back = gear 2.
Knob toward the tail = rotors (A) and doors (C); toward the nose = ramp (B) and winch (D). Our list has A and B the other way round.
Left lever: tip down = drive, up = crane. Right lever: tip up = slewing and winch, down = outriggers and boom.
Lever position 1 = doors, position 2 = engine cover. (Claude looked at these two pages: the inset is numbered 1 and 2.)

waiting.title: Two audit rows where booklet and file agree on what the function is
waiting.what: Changes to our function lists. The trial could not move these, because our reading still holds the parts rigid. The file's parts match the booklet's description.

rows.says: Our list: the rear axle is sprung on two shock absorbers. The booklet: independent rear suspension, arms and hubs each side, with rockers and two crosswise shock absorbers, like the front.
Our list: four levers, in two pairs. The booklet: two levers, each in an H gate; left lever A or B, right lever C or D.
